slots.practicalActivity: Install Power BI Desktop (Microsoft Store or powerbi.microsoft.com) and, once it opens, spend 20 minutes clicking through every ribbon tab and the Report/Data/Model view icons without loading a file, building a mental map of where things live before you touch real data.
slots.deliverable: A working Power BI Desktop install, plus a short written note naming what each of Get Data, Transform, Model, Visualize, and Publish does in the Power BI workflow.

lessons.title: The Power BI Workflow: Get → Transform → Model → Visualize → Publish

slots.practicalActivity: Load Microsoft's built-in Financial Sample dataset (Get Data > Excel; it ships with Desktop, or search 'power bi financial sample download'), then build a first report: a bar chart of Sales by Country, a card showing total Profit, and a slicer on Segment.
slots.deliverable: A saved .pbix ('01-first-report.pbix') with one bar chart, one card, and one working slicer built from the Financial Sample data.

slots.practicalActivity: Connect to the Financial Sample twice through two different source types: once as the native Excel file, then export one sheet to CSV and reconnect to that CSV, comparing the auto-generated Source step between the two in Power Query Editor.
slots.deliverable: One .pbix with two separate queries ('FinancialSample_Excel' and 'FinancialSample_CSV') and a short written comparison of their Source steps.

lessons.title: Connecting to Web, JSON & REST API Data

slots.practicalActivity: If a SQL Server instance with a sample database is available, connect to one table via Get Data > SQL Server; otherwise connect to a free public JSON API (e.g. https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users) via Get Data > Web, then decide and write down whether that specific connection should use Import or DirectQuery.
slots.deliverable: A working query against either a SQL table or a REST endpoint, plus a written Import-vs-DirectQuery decision with the reasoning behind it.

slots.practicalActivity: Without a lesson to follow, connect to one more source type you haven't used yet (a second CSV, a public API, or a folder of files) and load it alongside your existing queries, then write one paragraph comparing connection reliability and refresh behavior across all the source types you've now connected to in this chapter.
slots.deliverable: One additional query from a new source type loaded into the same .pbix, plus a written comparison covering every connection type used across Chapter 2.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Financial Sample query in Power Query Editor, read through every step already in the Query Settings pane, then manually correct the data type of at least 5 columns (Date to Date, Units Sold to Whole Number, Gross Sales to Fixed Decimal, etc.) and watch the Applied Steps list grow.
slots.deliverable: A query with your own 'Changed Type' step and a written list of the data type you assigned to each of the 5 columns.

slots.practicalActivity: Remove rows where Units Sold is blank or zero and filter out one Country, then edit a copy of the source Excel file to put a letter into a numeric-looking cell and practice Replace Values / Replace Errors to resolve it in the query.
slots.deliverable: A cleaned query with explicit 'Removed Rows', 'Filtered Rows', and 'Replaced Errors' steps visible in Applied Steps.

slots.practicalActivity: In a throwaway copy of the query, split a text column on a delimiter and extract the first 3 characters of Product into a new column, then add a Conditional Column labeling each row 'High Margin' or 'Low Margin' against a Gross Margin threshold you choose yourself.
slots.deliverable: A query with one split/extracted text column and one conditional column, with your margin threshold noted in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Duplicate the query, pivot Month Name into separate summed-Sales columns, then unpivot it back to confirm the round trip. Separately, use Group By to build a new summary table of total Sales and average Profit per Country.
slots.deliverable: A standalone summary query ('Sales_By_Country') built via Group By and kept separate from the main fact query.

slots.practicalActivity: Split the Financial Sample into two mock year-range tables in Excel, load both, and Append them into one stacked table. Separately, build a small Country-to-Region lookup table and Merge it into the main query as a new Region column.
slots.deliverable: One appended combined-years query and one merged query with a new Region column pulled from a separate lookup table.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Power Query Parameter (e.g. a MinUnitsSold threshold) and wire it into a filter step so editing the parameter changes which rows load. Then review every query built so far: rename cryptic step names, disable load on staging queries, and check for broken query folding.
slots.deliverable: A working parameter that changes filtered results when edited, plus a cleaned-up set of queries with renamed steps and non-essential queries set to not load.

slots.practicalActivity: Take a different raw public dataset (e.g. a sample orders export CSV) and, without lesson-by-lesson instructions, chain at least 6 Power Query techniques from this chapter on it in an order you choose: a data type fix, row filtering, a conditional column, a merge with a lookup table, a group-by summary, and a parameter.
slots.deliverable: An original cleaned query, built from a dataset you chose, demonstrating at least 6 distinct Power Query techniques chained end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the Financial Sample tables plus the Region lookup table from Chapter 3, classify each table in writing as fact or dimension, then arrange them in Model view with the fact table centered and dimension tables around it, approximating a star schema.
slots.deliverable: A written fact/dimension classification for at least 3 tables and a Model view layout with the fact table centered and dimensions arranged around it.

slots.practicalActivity: In Model view, draw a relationship from the Region lookup table to the fact table on the Country key, check and set its cardinality explicitly, then toggle cross-filter direction from single to both and observe the visual change on the relationship line before deciding which direction is correct.
slots.deliverable: A working relationship with cardinality and filter direction set deliberately, plus a one-sentence written justification for the final choice.

lessons.title: Building a Complete Power BI Data Model

slots.practicalActivity: Create a second relationship between two tables already connected elsewhere so it becomes inactive, inspect it in Model view, then finish a complete model with at least 3 dimension tables connected to the one fact table.
slots.deliverable: A complete data model in Model view with one fact table, at least 3 dimension tables, and one active plus one inactive relationship clearly visible.

slots.practicalActivity: Start a new .pbix, import a fresh dataset with at least 3 naturally related tables (orders, customers, products from any free sample retail dataset), and build a complete star schema on your own: classify fact vs. dimension tables, create every relationship, and set cardinality and filter direction deliberately.
slots.deliverable: A new .pbix ('04-model-review.pbix') with an original, correctly structured star schema model built without lesson-by-lesson guidance.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Chapter 4 model, open a new measure and type 3 original DAX expressions from scratch: a literal-number measure, a simple SUM measure, and a measure with an explanatory // comment.
slots.deliverable: 3 original, working measures demonstrating correct DAX syntax, written without copying the lesson's examples.

slots.practicalActivity: Create one calculated column on the fact table (e.g. a row-by-row Profit Margin % column) and one measure that aggregates something different (e.g. Average Order Value), using your own field names and logic.
slots.deliverable: One calculated column and one measure, both with original naming, validated in a table visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Without referring back to the lesson, write 5 new measures from scratch: Total Sales, Total Units, Average Order Value, Distinct Customer Count, and Max Single-Order Profit.
slots.deliverable: 5 original measures added to the model, each tested in a table visual to confirm the values look correct.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short explanation in your own words of why a calculated column recalculates per row at refresh while a measure recalculates per filter context at query time, then build 2 new aggregation measures using COUNTROWS and DISTINCTCOUNT on columns you haven't used yet.
slots.deliverable: A short written comparison plus 2 new aggregation measures, validated in a visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a matrix visual by Country and Year, then write an original CALCULATE measure of your own design (e.g. Sales for one specific Country regardless of the row's own Country) next to a plain SUM measure to directly observe filter context being overridden.
slots.deliverable: A working CALCULATE-based measure shown in a matrix beside a plain SUM measure, with a written note on which filter it overrides.

slots.practicalActivity: Drill practice: write 4 original CALCULATE measures, each overriding a different filter (one by Country, one by Year, one by Segment, one combining two conditions with AND logic inside CALCULATE), and place all 4 side by side in one table visual.
slots.deliverable: A table visual showing 4 distinct CALCULATE-based measures with visibly different, explainable results.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a calculated column that references a measure to trigger context transition, write down the value you expected versus what you got and why, then write 2 original SUMX measures (e.g. a weighted-profit calculation and a custom row-level calculation not shown in the lesson).
slots.deliverable: One demonstrated context-transition example with a written explanation, plus 2 original SUMX measures cross-checked by hand.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 original measures using CALCULATE filter modifiers (one with KEEPFILTERS, one with REMOVEFILTERS/ALL on a specific column) and one original measure using FILTER() for a table filter expression (e.g. Sales for orders above the average order value), using your own thresholds.
slots.deliverable: 3 original measures, each validated in a card or table visual with sensible, explainable numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: Timed drill: in 45 minutes, write 6 new measures combining iterators and FILTER with no lesson reference, then check each against a manually calculated expected value in a second table visual.
slots.deliverable: 6 original measures built under time pressure, each cross-checked against an independently calculated expected value.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original ALL-based measure (e.g. a % of Total Sales using SUM divided by an ALL-wrapped SUM) and an original ALLEXCEPT measure (e.g. a subtotal that ignores everything except Country), then build a visual showing ALLSELECTED behaving differently from ALL once a slicer is applied.
slots.deliverable: 3 original measures (ALL, ALLEXCEPT, ALLSELECTED) in one visual, with a written note on where ALLSELECTED's result differs from ALL's.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick your 3 messiest measures from this chapter and refactor them using VAR/RETURN for readability and to avoid repeated calculations, following DAX naming best practices.
slots.deliverable: 3 refactored measures using VAR/RETURN that produce identical results to their original versions, confirmed side by side.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a 'measure library' table visual listing every measure written this chapter (15+) with its current result, then clean up the Fields pane by deleting or organizing unused test measures into display folders.
slots.deliverable: An organized measure library visual plus a trimmed Fields pane with unused test measures removed or filed into folders.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, design and build 5 brand-new DAX measures for a business question you invent (e.g. 'what is our profit concentration risk?'), using at least one CALCULATE, one iterator function, and one ALL-family function across the 5 combined.
slots.deliverable: 5 original business-driven measures covering CALCULATE, an iterator, and an ALL-family function, with a one-paragraph explanation of the business question each answers.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Date table using CALENDAR or CALENDARAUTO typed from scratch, mark it as a Date table in Model view, add Year/Month Name/Quarter calculated columns, and relate it to the fact table's order date.
slots.deliverable: A marked Date table joined to the fact table, with Year, Month Name, and Quarter calculated columns written from scratch.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original DATEADD measure comparing Sales to the same period last year, then write 3 original time-intelligence measures of your own (YTD Sales, MTD Units, QTD Profit) using the Date table.
slots.deliverable: 4 original time-intelligence measures shown correctly in a line chart with a date-axis slicer.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original measure using DATESYTD or TOTALYTD with a custom fiscal year-end date, and one measure using DATESBETWEEN for a specific custom date range relevant to your dataset.
slots.deliverable: 2 original measures (one fiscal-YTD, one DATESBETWEEN range) validated against manually counted expected values.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a single Time Intelligence Dashboard page combining this chapter's measures: a line chart of YTD Sales vs. prior-year YTD, a card showing QTD Profit, and a year slicer that lets you confirm every measure recalculates correctly.
slots.deliverable: A working dashboard page where changing the year slicer correctly recalculates every time-intelligence measure without errors.

slots.practicalActivity: For 3 different business questions (trend over time, comparison across categories, single KPI), choose and justify a visual type for each in writing, then build a Table and a Matrix visual showing Sales by Country and Year with subtotals enabled.
slots.deliverable: A written justification for 3 visual-type choices, plus a working Table and Matrix visual with subtotals enabled.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a bar chart, a line chart, and a pie chart using field combinations you haven't used in earlier slots, then add a Card showing a KPI you pick and a Slicer that filters all 3 charts at once.
slots.deliverable: A report page with 3 distinct chart types plus a card and slicer, all cross-filtering correctly when the slicer is used.

slots.practicalActivity: Apply conditional formatting to a table (a color scale on Profit Margin, icons on a performance column) using thresholds you set yourself, then configure the Filter pane with one visual-level filter and one page-level filter with different logic.
slots.deliverable: A table with custom conditional formatting rules, and a report page with at least one visual-level and one page-level filter configured.

slots.practicalActivity: Edit visual interactions between two visuals on a page (change one from filter to highlight), then set up a drill-down hierarchy (Year > Quarter > Month) on a chart and a drillthrough page that opens filtered to a selected Country.
slots.deliverable: A page with customized visual interactions plus a working drill-down hierarchy and a functioning drillthrough page.

slots.practicalActivity: Add 2 buttons wired to bookmarks that toggle between two views of the same page (e.g. a Summary vs. Detail state), then add a trend line or forecast to an existing chart using a forecast length you choose yourself.
slots.deliverable: 2 working bookmark-driven buttons that toggle report state, plus a chart with a trend/forecast line configured with a custom forecast length.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original, fully interactive report page combining at least 6 techniques from this chapter without lesson guidance: your own visual choices, conditional formatting, a working filter, customized interactions, a drillthrough, and a bookmark-driven button.
slots.deliverable: A single polished report page demonstrating at least 6 distinct Chapter 7 techniques working together, built from your own design decisions.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page business requirements brief for an invented stakeholder (e.g. 'VP of Sales wants to track regional performance'), listing their top 3 questions, then choose and justify 4 specific KPIs that answer those questions using fields already in your model.
slots.deliverable: A written requirements brief with 3 stakeholder questions and a justified list of 4 KPIs mapped to your data model's fields.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch a dashboard wireframe applying visual hierarchy principles (most important KPI top-left, F-pattern reading order), then write a 3-sentence 'data story' narrative the dashboard should tell a viewer at a glance.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard wireframe sketch with annotated visual hierarchy, plus a written 3-sentence narrative statement.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the executive dashboard the wireframe describes: one page, 4-6 visuals max, a consistent color theme, and the 4 chosen KPIs prominent at the top, following the planned visual hierarchy.
slots.deliverable: A finished, polished one-page executive dashboard .pbix matching the earlier wireframe and KPI selections.

slots.practicalActivity: If a Power BI Service account is available (a free trial is enough), sign in and compare the Service web UI to Desktop side by side, listing 5 things you can only do in one or the other. Research which license tier (Free, Pro, Premium/Fabric capacity) your scenario would need and justify the choice.
slots.deliverable: A written 5-item comparison list (Desktop-only vs. Service-only capabilities) and a one-paragraph license recommendation.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new workspace in Power BI Service (or write out the exact steps if no license is available), then publish the Chapter 8 executive dashboard .pbix to that workspace using Desktop's Publish button.
slots.deliverable: The executive dashboard report live in a Power BI Service workspace, or a detailed step-by-step walkthrough document if publishing isn't available.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Service, locate the semantic model (dataset) behind the published report and review its settings, then share the report under a test scenario (a view-only link or a simulated colleague) and configure its access permissions.
slots.deliverable: A documented semantic model settings review plus a configured sharing/permissions setup for the published report.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Power BI App from the workspace (or document the steps), then create a standalone Service dashboard by pinning 3 tiles from the report to it, including at least one tile pinned as a live-updating tile.
slots.deliverable: A Power BI App containing the workspace content, and a Service dashboard with 3 pinned tiles from the report.

slots.practicalActivity: Without a lesson to follow, take the App and Service dashboard just built and tighten them for a real audience: rename the App to something a stakeholder would recognize, reorder its content list, resize and relabel the 3 pinned dashboard tiles, and write a one-paragraph note on who in an organization should receive Viewer vs. Member access to this workspace.
slots.deliverable: A relabeled, reordered Power BI App and dashboard ready to hand to a stakeholder, plus a written Viewer-vs-Member access recommendation.

slots.practicalActivity: Diagram how refresh works end to end for an Import-mode dataset: source change → gateway → Service → report. If a local data source and gateway access are available, install and register the on-premises data gateway.
slots.deliverable: A written refresh-flow diagram/explanation, plus a registered data gateway if your environment allows it, or documented installation steps if it doesn't.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure a daily scheduled refresh for the published dataset in the Service, then deliberately break it (point to a renamed/missing file or revoke a credential) and use the Service's refresh history and error message to diagnose the failure.
slots.deliverable: A configured scheduled refresh setting, plus a written troubleshooting log describing one real or simulated refresh failure and how it was diagnosed.

slots.practicalActivity: On the star-schema model, create 2 original RLS roles that each restrict the fact table to a different Country or Segment using a DAX filter expression written from scratch.
slots.deliverable: 2 working RLS roles defined in Modeling > Manage Roles, each with an original DAX filter condition, tested using 'View As Roles' in Desktop.

slots.practicalActivity: Publish the model with RLS roles to the Service and assign a test role to a user or group (or document the exact steps if admin access isn't available), then convert one static role into a dynamic RLS role driven by USERPRINCIPALNAME() against a user-mapping table built from scratch.
slots.deliverable: A dynamic RLS role using USERPRINCIPALNAME() tested with 'View As Roles', plus documented or completed steps for assigning roles to users in the Service.

slots.practicalActivity: Apply the dynamic RLS role to a more complex scenario: a table 2 relationship-hops away from the user-mapping table, verifying the filter still propagates correctly and adjusting bidirectional filtering or adding a bridge table as needed.
slots.deliverable: A verified RLS test case where the security filter correctly restricts data on a table not directly related to the security table, with a written note on what had to change in the model.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original RLS scenario end to end without lesson guidance: design a new role, write its DAX filter, test it with View As, and document how it would behave once published to the Service for a real team you invent.
slots.deliverable: One fully original, tested RLS role with written documentation of its design rationale and expected Service behavior.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short requirements document for a capstone dashboard (e.g. a regional sales performance dashboard), listing the stakeholder, their top 3 questions, and required KPIs, then import the raw data needed (a multi-table dataset with at least orders, products, customers, and dates).
slots.deliverable: A written capstone requirements brief, plus all raw source tables successfully loaded into a new .pbix ('12-capstone.pbix').

slots.practicalActivity: In Power Query, clean and transform every raw table (fix data types, remove errors, handle blanks), then build a proper star schema in Model view with one fact table and the appropriate dimension tables, setting relationships and cardinality deliberately.
slots.deliverable: A cleaned set of queries and a complete star-schema data model in the capstone .pbix, verified in Model view.

slots.practicalActivity: Continue building: add a Date table to the capstone model (via CALENDAR/CALENDARAUTO), relate it properly, and double-check every relationship's cardinality and filter direction before moving on to DAX.
slots.deliverable: A capstone model with a working, related Date table and a fully reviewed relationship diagram with no unintended many-to-many or inactive relationships.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the core DAX measures the requirements brief calls for (at least 6: a few basic aggregations, at least one CALCULATE-based measure, and one time-intelligence measure), then build the main report page with the primary visuals needed to answer the stakeholder's top 3 questions.
slots.deliverable: At least 6 working, original DAX measures and a report page with the primary visuals answering the stated business questions.

slots.practicalActivity: Polish the report: apply consistent formatting and a color theme, add conditional formatting to at least one visual, and clean up titles, labels, and tooltips so the page reads clearly to someone seeing it for the first time.
slots.deliverable: A visually polished report page with consistent formatting, conditional formatting on at least one visual, and clear titles/labels.

slots.practicalActivity: Add interactivity to the capstone report (a drillthrough page, a bookmark-driven toggle, or a drill-down hierarchy matching the requirements), then publish the finished report to a Power BI Service workspace (or document the exact publish steps if unavailable).
slots.deliverable: A capstone report with at least one interactivity feature, published to the Service or with documented publish steps completed.

slots.practicalActivity: QA pass: test every measure and visual against at least 2 known filter combinations and manually verify the numbers are correct, then test the published report's refresh and confirm the data source credentials and refresh schedule are configured.
slots.deliverable: A written QA checklist with at least 4 verified test cases, and a confirmed scheduled refresh configuration on the published dataset.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure RLS on the capstone model matching the stakeholder scenario (e.g. restrict a regional manager role to their region) and confirm the scheduled refresh still works with security applied, then prepare and rehearse a 5-minute presentation of the final dashboard.
slots.deliverable: A working RLS role applied to the capstone model with refresh still functioning, plus presentation notes for a 5-minute final dashboard walkthrough.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliver the final presentation of the capstone dashboard (to a peer, mentor, or recorded for yourself): walk through the business requirement, the data model decisions, the key DAX measures, and the finished dashboard, then note 2 things you'd improve with more time.
slots.deliverable: A completed capstone presentation (live or recorded) covering requirements, model, measures, and final dashboard, plus a written list of 2 concrete improvements for a 'v2'.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can independently connect to and clean real business data in Power Query, build a proper star-schema data model, write their own DAX measures and time-intelligence calculations, and design, publish, secure, and present a polished, interactive Power BI dashboard end to end.
